question: What is the minimum age an individual must be before the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA) may issue a real estate broker, associate broker, or salesperson license?
choice_a: 21 years old
choice_b: 19 years old
choice_c: There is no statutory minimum age
choice_d: 18 years old
explanation: MCL 339.2502a(1) states that the department shall not issue a license to an individual who is under the age of 18 years. This minimum applies uniformly to broker, associate broker, and salesperson applicants.
source_note: MCL 339.2502a(1) (independently confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: How many total clock hours of approved pre-licensure classroom education must a Michigan real estate broker applicant complete?
choice_a: 90 clock hours
choice_b: 40 clock hours
choice_c: 60 clock hours
choice_d: 120 clock hours
explanation: MCL 339.2504(1) requires a broker applicant to complete at least 90 clock hours of approved prelicensure classroom courses in real estate, more than double the 40-hour requirement for salesperson applicants.
source_note: MCL 339.2504(1) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Within the 90 clock hours of pre-licensure education required for a Michigan broker license, how many hours must specifically cover civil rights law and fair housing law?
choice_a: At least 4 clock hours
choice_b: At least 9 clock hours
choice_c: At least 6 clock hours
choice_d: At least 12 clock hours
explanation: MCL 339.2504(1) requires that at least 9 of the 90 broker prelicensure hours be instruction on civil rights law and fair housing law -- more than double the 4-hour civil rights/equal opportunity requirement built into the salesperson's 40-hour curriculum.
source_note: MCL 339.2504(1) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: A Michigan broker applicant who has never held an active salesperson license must have completed the required 90 hours of pre-licensure education within what window before applying?
choice_a: The 24-month period preceding the date of application
choice_b: The 12-month period preceding the date of application
choice_c: The 36-month period preceding the date of application
choice_d: There is no time limit on when the hours were completed
explanation: MCL 339.2504(1) requires the 90 hours to be completed within the 36-month period preceding the application date, unless the applicant held an active salesperson license during that entire period, in which case the timing restriction does not apply.
source_note: MCL 339.2504(1) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: A broker applicant held an active Michigan real estate salesperson license throughout the entire 3 years before applying, but completed her 90 hours of prelicensure coursework 5 years ago. Does the 36-month completion window disqualify her application?
choice_a: Yes, she must retake all 90 hours regardless of her salesperson license status
choice_b: No, because the timing window only applies to the civil rights portion of the coursework
choice_c: Yes, because the waiver only applies to associate broker applicants, not broker applicants
choice_d: No, because MCL 339.2504 waives the 36-month timing requirement for an applicant who held an active salesperson license throughout that period
explanation: MCL 339.2504(1) expressly exempts an applicant from the 36-month education-completion window if the applicant held an active salesperson license during that period, regardless of how long ago the coursework was originally completed.
source_note: MCL 339.2504(1) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: How much real estate experience must a Michigan broker applicant demonstrate under MCL 339.2505?
choice_a: The equivalent of 3 years of full-time experience in the business of real estate
choice_b: The equivalent of 2 years of full-time experience in the business of real estate
choice_c: The equivalent of 5 years of full-time experience in the business of real estate
choice_d: No experience is required if the applicant completes the 90-hour education requirement
explanation: MCL 339.2505 requires broker (and associate broker) applicants to demonstrate the equivalent of 3 years of full-time experience in the business of real estate, with the department awarding credit according to defined categories of qualifying work.
source_note: MCL 339.2505 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Under MCL 339.2505, how much experience credit toward the broker license does a licensed real estate salesperson earn for a 12-month period in which they closed at least 5 transactions?
choice_a: Six months of credit
choice_b: One year of credit
choice_c: Two years of credit
choice_d: No credit -- salespersons cannot use their sales activity toward the broker experience requirement
explanation: MCL 339.2505 grants a licensed real estate salesperson one year of experience credit for each 12-month period in which the salesperson closed at least 5 real estate transactions, one of several defined experience-credit pathways toward the 3-year broker requirement.
source_note: MCL 339.2505 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Under MCL 339.2505's experience-credit rules for a broker applicant who acted as an active real estate investor, what is the maximum credit obtainable through investor transactions alone?
choice_a: Three years, earned as one year's credit for each 5 property transactions
choice_b: Two years, with no cap on the number of transactions counted
choice_c: One year, earned as six months' credit for each 5 property transactions
choice_d: Investor transactions cannot be counted toward broker experience under any circumstances
explanation: MCL 339.2505 credits a real estate investor 6 months of experience for each 5 property transactions, but caps the total credit obtainable through this investor pathway at 1 year.
source_note: MCL 339.2505 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Besides licensed salespersons, builders, and investors, which other category of professional does MCL 339.2505 recognize as eligible for broker-experience credit based on transactional activity?
choice_a: A licensed home inspector who inspected at least 20 properties in a year
choice_b: A property insurance adjuster who processed at least 10 real estate-related claims in a year
choice_c: A notary public who notarized at least 15 real estate closing documents in a year
choice_d: An attorney who acted as attorney on at least 6 real estate transactions in a year, earning one year of credit
explanation: MCL 339.2505 grants an attorney one year of experience credit for each year in which the attorney acted as attorney on at least 6 real estate transactions; the statute also recognizes licensed appraisers, loan officers, and title company officers who worked the equivalent of 40+ hours/week for 48+ weeks/year.
source_note: MCL 339.2505 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Which of the following is an absolute statutory bar to receiving a Michigan real estate broker license under MCL 339.2505, regardless of the applicant's education and experience?
choice_a: A prior conviction for embezzlement or misappropriation of funds
choice_b: A prior misdemeanor traffic citation
choice_c: Having declared personal bankruptcy more than 5 years earlier
choice_d: Having previously worked as an unlicensed real estate assistant
explanation: MCL 339.2505 bars licensure for an applicant who has been convicted of embezzlement or misappropriation of funds; the department may also require satisfactory proof of the applicant's business experience, competence, and good moral character generally.
source_note: MCL 339.2505 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: How does Michigan law define an "associate real estate broker" under MCL 339.2501?
choice_a: An individual who has passed only the national portion of the broker exam but not the Michigan-specific portion
choice_b: An individual who meets all broker licensure requirements but is licensed to provide real estate brokerage services as an employee or independent contractor of a real estate broker
choice_c: A salesperson who has completed 40 hours of continuing education but not the full broker curriculum
choice_d: A broker who supervises other brokers within a multi-office brokerage
explanation: MCL 339.2501 defines an associate real estate broker as an individual who meets the broker licensure requirements of the article and is licensed under section 2505 to provide brokerage services as an employee or independent contractor of a real estate broker -- the same qualification standard as a broker, but a different working arrangement.
source_note: MCL 339.2501 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: What is the fundamental difference in Michigan between a "real estate broker" license and an "associate real estate broker" license?
choice_a: An associate broker has met a lower experience threshold than a full broker
choice_b: An associate broker is only permitted to handle residential transactions, while a full broker may handle commercial transactions
choice_c: Both require the same education, experience, and examination, but an associate broker practices as an employee or independent contractor under a broker rather than operating independently
choice_d: An associate broker license is temporary and automatically converts to a full broker license after 3 years
explanation: Under MCL 339.2501 and 339.2505, associate broker and broker applicants meet identical qualification standards (education, experience, examination); the distinction is one of working arrangement -- a broker may operate independently, while an associate broker functions as an employee or independent contractor under a licensed broker.
source_note: MCL 339.2501; MCL 339.2505 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Under MCL 339.2501, what conditions must be satisfied for an associate broker or salesperson to be treated as an independent contractor of the employing broker rather than an employee?
choice_a: The associate broker or salesperson must have at least 5 years of licensure and file a separate business registration with LARA
choice_b: A written agreement alone is sufficient; there is no compensation-source requirement
choice_c: At least 50% of annual compensation must be commission, with no written agreement required
choice_d: A written agreement stating the broker does not consider them an employee for tax purposes, AND at least 75% of their annual compensation from the broker is commission from real estate sales
explanation: MCL 339.2501 requires both: (1) a written agreement in which the broker does not treat the associate broker or salesperson as an employee for federal and state income tax purposes, and (2) at least 75% of the annual compensation paid to that individual is derived from real estate sales commissions.
source_note: MCL 339.2501 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Under MCL 339.2503, an owner who sells a detached single-family dwelling, duplex, triplex, or quadruplex that has never been occupied is exempt from real estate licensure requirements under what condition?
choice_a: The dwelling was built by the owner while the owner held a license under article 24 (the state construction/builder licensing article)
choice_b: The owner has resided in Michigan for at least 10 years
choice_c: The property is sold for less than $200,000
choice_d: The sale occurs through a licensed title company
explanation: MCL 339.2503(1) exempts an owner selling a never-before-occupied detached single-family dwelling, duplex, triplex, or quadruplex from real estate licensure, but only if the property was built while the owner was licensed under article 24 of the Occupational Code.
source_note: MCL 339.2503(1) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Which of the following individuals is generally exempt from Michigan real estate broker/salesperson licensure when handling their own property, unless doing so becomes their principal vocation?
choice_a: A licensed contractor performing repairs on a property they do not own
choice_b: An owner or lessor (or their attorney-in-fact) performing licensed acts regarding property they themselves own or lease
choice_c: A property management company managing units on behalf of multiple unrelated owners
choice_d: A mortgage loan officer originating loans for unrelated third-party buyers
explanation: MCL 339.2503(1) exempts owners and lessors (or their attorneys-in-fact) from licensure when performing broker/salesperson-type acts regarding their own property, unless that activity constitutes their principal vocation, at which point licensure is required.
source_note: MCL 339.2503(1) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Under MCL 339.2503, which professionals are exempt from real estate licensure when acting within the scope of their own professional duties, such as selling property under court order?
choice_a: Licensed home appraisers performing valuations for a mortgage lender
choice_b: Certified public accountants preparing a seller's closing statement
choice_c: Attorneys-at-law rendering legal services, and receivers, trustees in bankruptcy, administrators, and executors selling real estate under order of a court
choice_d: Insurance agents selling title insurance policies
explanation: MCL 339.2503(2) exempts attorneys-at-law rendering legal services, as well as receivers, trustees in bankruptcy, administrators, and executors selling real estate under order of a court, from real estate licensure for that activity.
source_note: MCL 339.2503(2) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: A trustee selling property under a deed of trust makes repeated, successive sales without going through a licensed broker. Under MCL 339.2503, is this activity exempt from licensure?
choice_a: Yes -- all trustee sales under a deed of trust are exempt regardless of frequency
choice_b: Yes, but only if the trustee is also a licensed attorney
choice_c: No license is ever required for any trustee sale in Michigan
choice_d: No -- the deed-of-trust exemption does not extend to a trustee making repeated or successive sales outside a licensed broker
explanation: MCL 339.2503(2) exempts a trustee selling under a deed of trust, but that exemption does not cover a trustee who makes repeated or successive sales outside the involvement of a licensed broker -- such activity falls back under the licensing requirement.
source_note: MCL 339.2503(2) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Persons already regulated under Michigan's mortgage brokers, lenders, and servicers licensing act (1987 PA 173) are exempt from real estate broker/salesperson licensure under MCL 339.2503 under what limitation?
choice_a: Only so long as they do not perform other acts that independently require real estate licensure
choice_b: Only if they also hold a Michigan attorney license
choice_c: The exemption is unconditional and covers any real estate activity they undertake
choice_d: Only for transactions involving commercial, not residential, property
explanation: MCL 339.2503(3) exempts persons regulated under the mortgage brokers, lenders, and servicers licensing act from real estate licensure, but only to the extent they don't also perform other acts (such as listing or selling real estate) that would independently require a real estate license.
source_note: MCL 339.2503(3) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: How many total clock hours of continuing education must a Michigan real estate licensee complete in each 3-year license cycle under the pre-existing rules referenced in MCL 339.2504a?
choice_a: 12 clock hours
choice_b: 18 clock hours
choice_c: 24 clock hours
choice_d: 9 clock hours
explanation: MCL 339.2504a requires a licensee to complete at least 18 clock hours of eligible continuing education courses in each license cycle under the rules in effect before newer department rules take effect (a figure consistent with the statute's own alternate formula of 6 hours per year of the license cycle).
source_note: MCL 339.2504a (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Within each year of a Michigan real estate license cycle, MCL 339.2504a requires the licensee's continuing education to include a minimum number of hours on which specific subject?
choice_a: At least 5 hours on real estate finance and mortgage lending
choice_b: At least 3 hours on property valuation and appraisal methods
choice_c: At least 2 hours on laws, rules, and court cases regarding real estate, plus at least 1 hour on compliance with fair housing law
choice_d: There is no subject-specific minimum -- any 18 hours of approved coursework satisfies the requirement
explanation: MCL 339.2504a requires that, within each year of the license cycle, a licensee complete not less than 2 hours of courses on laws, rules, and court cases regarding real estate, and not less than 1 hour of courses on compliance with local, state, or federal fair housing laws.
source_note: MCL 339.2504a (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Under MCL 339.2504a, may the department prorate the continuing education hours required of a licensee whose license was newly issued partway through a license cycle?
choice_a: No -- every new licensee must complete the full 18 hours regardless of when in the cycle the license was issued
choice_b: No -- new licensees are entirely exempt from continuing education until their second license cycle
choice_c: Proration is available only for salespersons, not for brokers or associate brokers
choice_d: Yes -- the department may prorate the number of continuing education hours required for the year in which the license is issued
explanation: MCL 339.2504a permits the department to prorate the continuing education hours a newly licensed individual must complete for the partial year of the license cycle during which the license was issued.
source_note: MCL 339.2504a (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Under MCL 339.2504a, does repeating a continuing education course a licensee has already completed generate additional credit hours toward the renewal requirement?
choice_a: No -- repeating a previously completed course does not earn additional hours toward the continuing education requirement
choice_b: Yes -- a repeated course counts double toward the total hours required
choice_c: Yes, but only if at least 5 years have passed since the course was first taken
choice_d: Repetition is prohibited outright and results in denial of the license renewal
explanation: MCL 339.2504a specifically provides that repeating a previously completed course does not earn the licensee additional hours toward the continuing education requirement, preventing licensees from satisfying their hour requirement by re-taking the same course.
source_note: MCL 339.2504a (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: hedge: Michigan real estate licenses are generally described as renewing on what recurring cycle, consistent with the 3-year period used in MCL 339.2504a's continuing-education formula (years in cycle x 6 hours = 18 hours)?
choice_a: Annually (every 1 year)
choice_b: Triennially (every 3 years)
choice_c: Every 2 years
choice_d: Every 5 years
explanation: hedge: the 3-year license cycle length itself is set by administrative rule (Mich. Admin. Code R 339.1003a, triennial license renewal/expiration) rather than spelled out directly in the article 25 statutory text reviewed here, but it is corroborated by MCL 339.2504a's own math (18 required hours equals 6 hours per year over a 3-year cycle).
source_note: hedge: Mich. Admin. Code R 339.1003a (secondary source, not independently fetched from legislature.mi.gov in full); corroborated by MCL 339.2504a's 3-year-cycle arithmetic

question: Under MCL 339.2506, what must a Michigan real estate licensee do if their business location changes?
choice_a: Nothing -- location changes do not need to be reported unless the license is also being renewed
choice_b: Reapply for licensure from the beginning, including the examination
choice_c: Notify the department in writing of the change
choice_d: Notify only the local municipality's business licensing office, not LARA
explanation: MCL 339.2506 requires a licensee to notify the department in writing of any change in business location, keeping LARA's licensing records current.
source_note: MCL 339.2506 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Under MCL 339.2506, when a salesperson or associate broker changes employing brokers, how long is the transfer period during which their pocket card serves as valid evidence of licensure, provided the transfer application is complete and the new broker is licensed?
choice_a: 30 days
choice_b: 60 days
choice_c: 90 days
choice_d: 45 days
explanation: MCL 339.2506 establishes a 45-day transfer period during which a salesperson's or associate broker's pocket card is valid evidence of licensure while changing employing brokers, so long as the transfer application is complete and the new broker holds a valid license.
source_note: MCL 339.2506 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Under MCL 339.2506, upon suspension or revocation of a license, what must the affected licensee do with their pocket card and license?
choice_a: Immediately return the pocket card and license to the department
choice_b: Retain them until the next scheduled renewal date
choice_c: Destroy them personally and certify destruction in writing
choice_d: Transfer them to their employing broker for safekeeping
explanation: MCL 339.2506 requires a licensee whose license has been suspended or revoked to immediately return the pocket card and license to the department.
source_note: MCL 339.2506 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Under MCL 339.2507, when a real estate salesperson's employment with a broker is terminated, what must the broker do with the department within 5 days?
choice_a: File a written explanation of the reason for termination with the department
choice_b: Deliver or mail by certified mail the salesperson's license to the department
choice_c: Notify the salesperson's E&O insurance carrier
choice_d: Post a public notice of the termination in the local courthouse
explanation: MCL 339.2507 requires the broker to deliver or mail by certified mail the terminated salesperson's license to the department within 5 days of termination, and to notify the salesperson in writing at their last known address that this has been done.
source_note: MCL 339.2507 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Under MCL 339.2507, after a real estate salesperson's employment is terminated and their license is surrendered to the department, may the salesperson continue to perform licensed real estate acts under the authority of that license?
choice_a: Yes, for up to 45 days while a transfer to a new broker is pending
choice_b: Yes, so long as the acts are limited to open houses already scheduled before termination
choice_c: No -- a salesperson shall not perform an act regulated by article 25, directly or indirectly, under authority of that license after the date of termination
choice_d: Yes, if the former broker provides written permission
explanation: MCL 339.2507 prohibits a terminated salesperson from performing any act regulated by article 25, directly or indirectly, under authority of the surrendered license after the date of termination -- distinct from the 45-day pocket-card transfer allowance in MCL 339.2506, which applies while an application to transfer to a new broker is pending, not after simple termination without a pending transfer.
source_note: MCL 339.2507; contrasted with MCL 339.2506 (both confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Under MCL 339.2507, how many active real estate salesperson licenses may the department issue to the same individual for the same period of time?
choice_a: Up to 2, if sponsored by different brokers
choice_b: Up to 3, one per brokerage the salesperson is affiliated with
choice_c: There is no limit
choice_d: No more than 1
explanation: MCL 339.2507 provides that the department shall not issue more than 1 license to a real estate salesperson for the same period of time, preventing a salesperson from holding concurrent, duplicate salesperson licenses.
source_note: MCL 339.2507 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

question: Under MCL 339.2504, what alternative may allow an applicant to substitute for part of the standard prelicensure classroom-hour requirement?
choice_a: The department may recognize certain degrees in law, business, or finance as equivalent to completion of prelicensure classroom hours
choice_b: Any bachelor's degree in any field automatically satisfies the full 90-hour requirement
choice_c: Five years of unrelated full-time work experience automatically substitutes for the classroom hours
choice_d: There is no substitute; every applicant must complete the classroom hours regardless of education background
explanation: MCL 339.2504(1)(b)(iv) allows the department to determine that certain degrees in law, business, or finance may substitute for completion of the required prelicensure classroom hours, rather than requiring every applicant to sit through the full classroom curriculum.
source_note: MCL 339.2504(1)(b)(iv) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)
